status: PLANNED: recorded and committed before any probe request
purpose: Check that Binance Spot 1h klines return the aggregated trading-activity fields (base volume, quote volume, number of trades, taker-buy base and taker-buy quote volume) with the documented schema at three sampled dates. Feasibility only: no return, outcome, label, model, strategy or relation between activity and price is computed.
authorization: Owner task of 2026-11-26: public market data without credentials; v1's 20 pairs; 24 closed 1h candles from 00:00 UTC on each of three dates; at most 60 kline requests, excluding rate-limit retries. No account, Supabase or production access; no full-history download.

endpoint.why: The host v1 and src/lib/binance.ts already use, so the source is unchanged. No credentials. No X-MBX-TIME-UNIT header, so times are milliseconds. No timeZone parameter, so intervals are UTC.
endpoint.documentedIpLimit: REQUEST_WEIGHT 6000 per minute per IP (rest-api.md, exchangeInfo example)

datesRelativeToV1: All three lie inside v1's examined history: v1's first decision day (train), the first day of v1's validation period, and the last day before v1's cutoff (test). Any value retrieved here is examined-period data, never untouched evidence.
order: Pairs in the order above; for each pair the three dates in chronological order. One request at a time, at least 250 ms apart.

stopRules.http429: Wait Retry-After seconds (stop if absent or above 120) and retry that request once; the retry does not count toward the 60. A second 429 stops the probe.
stopRules.http403or451: Stop the probe. No other host, proxy, header or credential is tried.
stopRules.usedWeight: Stop if X-MBX-USED-WEIGHT-1M exceeds 3000, half the documented limit.
stopRules.otherFailure: Any other status, timeout or network error is recorded, not retried, and the probe continues with the next request.

storage.directory: .zerochart-market-data/binance-activity-probe-2026-11-26/ (git-ignored, new, write-once; the probe refuses to run if it exists)
storage.raw: raw/<SYMBOL>-<date>.json: each 200 response body, byte for byte
storage.manifest: manifest.json: plan SHA-256, commit, per-request URL, status, retrieval time, X-MBX-USED-WEIGHT-1M, byte count and SHA-256
storage.validation: validation.json: the checks below, per request and in total
storage.v1: .zerochart-market-data/spot-24h-v1/ is opened read-only for an OHLC parity check. It is never written, renamed or supplemented.

checks: Response is a JSON array of 24 rows; each row has exactly 12 fields.
Open time (0) and close time (6) are integers; open times are startTime + i × 3,600,000 for i = 0 … 23, in order, without duplicates; close time = open time + 3,599,999.
Every candle closed before the request was sent.
Open, high, low, close (1–4) are positive decimal strings; high ≥ open, close, low; low ≤ open, close.
Base volume (5), quote volume (7), taker-buy base (9) and taker-buy quote (10) are nonnegative decimal strings; number of trades (8) is a nonnegative safe integer; field 11 is reported as found.
Taker-buy base ≤ base volume and taker-buy quote ≤ quote volume, compared as exact decimals.
Zero consistency: number of trades is 0 exactly when base volume is 0, and then quote and taker-buy volumes are 0.

Implied mean prices, quote ÷ base and taker-buy quote ÷ taker-buy base (when the denominator is positive), lie within [low, high] with a relative tolerance of 1e-6 for rounding. This is an inference from the field names (every trade in the hour priced within its range), not a documented guarantee.
OHLC parity with v1: Number.parseFloat of fields 1–4 equals v1's saved open, high, low and close for the same open time, and close time equals v1's closeTime.

classification.validZero: A row that passes every check with base volume 0 and trades 0 (an hour without trades).
classification.missing: An expected hour with no row, a row shorter than 12 fields, or a null field.
classification.invalid: A present field that fails a type, range, ordering, inequality or consistency check.

notComputed: No return, outcome, label, indicator, model, correlation, ranking or profitability figure. Summary statistics are limited to counts and the range of taker-buy share needed to show the inequality checks.
limitations: 60 pair-days demonstrate availability at these sampled dates only. They cannot establish complete historical coverage, that values never change after retrieval (point-in-time archival availability), or how Binance computes the fields.
